## This week
The vault exhaled. After the heaviest two-week intake stretch since launch (50+ notes between Mar 16-21), this week brought just 17 items in seven days — four of those days had zero or one clip. But the one burst day mattered. On the 26th, twelve items landed in a single session: three Toby Shorin essays introducing social forms and body futurism as a genuinely new intellectual thread, Jill Lepore's New Yorker piece framing AI constitutionalism as democratic failure, Karpathy's autoresearch repo and No Priors interview, PostHog's agent harness retrospective, and Will Wright's decade-long quest to build a mind-simulation game. Note: the week of Mar 17-22 had no weekly synthesis (the chain didn't fire). ## Disconnected clusters sharing implicit themes

1. **Social forms + governance** — Shorin's theory of social forms (structured arrangements of people, distinct from institutions) and the governance assertion are circling the same problem from opposite ends. Shorin from phenomenology and culture; you from protocols and engineering. The bridge is "protocolism" but nobody has written it.

2. **Thompson Sampling + signal queue** — Tyler Folkman's content curation piece (two numbers per source, Beta distribution, feedback loop) is a direct upgrade for the signal queue's static scoring formula. Thompson Sampling would let the system learn which content types you actually engage with. The connection is obvious and unconnected.

3. **Neuroscience of attention + calm technology** — The restless-by-design piece (DMN, variable-ratio reinforcement, friction removal) is the scientific backing for why the signal queue and calm technology thesis exist. The brain's default mode network surfaces unresolved material; scrolling exploits the same dopamine loop. This connects the vault's design philosophy to its content.

4. **Agent infra (OpenClaw stubs) + agentic commerce (Visa)** — Five OpenClaw stubs (zeroboot, canopy, clawrouter, clawflows, AGENT-ZERO) describe the compute substrate; Visa's agentic commerce describes the payment rails above. The middle layer — what agents actually do and who authorizes it — is the governance assertion's territory.

5. **Will Wright's Proxi + vault as reflection engine** — Wright spent a decade building a game simulating the player's mind from memories. The vault surfaces patterns from captured thinking. Both use the user's own cognition as substrate. The connection is implicit and unexamined.
